title: fix(wire): cut DXF arcs and circles as true arcs
body:
## What changed

A Wire Contour on a selected DXF chain with an arc or a circle now cuts. The wire path holds true arcs. The generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM wire posts write them as G2 / G3 with incremental I J. An exact straight polygon keeps the polygon path of #3180, byte for byte.

### Motion (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/`)

- New `arc_span.rs`, `arc_chain.rs`: the closed line / arc / circle chain in world XY, walked counter-clockwise. The joint gap tolerance is `JOINT_TOL` = 0.25 µm. A wider gap is refused by name.
- New `arc_offset.rs`: the analytic offset. Each line moves along its normal. Each arc becomes a concentric arc. A pivot arc of the kerf radius about the drawing corner closes each outside corner. A trim at the meet of the two parallels closes each inside corner.
- Refusals by name, never a clamp:
- New `arc_cut.rs` (`wire_contour_arcs`): a straight lead to the nearest path point. On a circle the lead is radial. A full circle (or an arc of more than half a turn) is cut as two halves. Each arc goes onto its CL lattice centre (1e-6 mm) with its radius kept. If the centre move, the joint gap and the near-tangent miss together pass 1 nm, the path moves that far to the waste side, and a path note says so.
- New `arc_laws.rs`: the kerf law and the cover law read the drawing itself. The kerf law uses the exact least distance from each recorded move (line, or arc about its lattice centre) to each line and arc of the chain. `laws.rs` only moves the cover refusal text into `uncovered()` (no behaviour change).

### Sim verifier (`crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`)

- New `arcs.rs`: an XY arc move of a vertical cut is read as chords of at most 25 nm sagitta (`ARC_SAG`). Each chord reading is reduced by the chord's sagitta, so an arc whose kerf enters the product never passes.
- An arc on a leaning wire (taper) stays unreadable by name. A tabbed cut with arcs is unreadable by name.

### App (`crates/app/src/operation/`)

- `wire_sketch.rs`: the arc refusal and the exact-gap refusal are removed. `check_path` accepts XY arcs and bounds them by their axis extremes.
- New `wire_sketch_arcs.rs`: routes each chain that is not an exact polygon to `wire_contour_arcs`. The verifier gets the product as a waste-side ring of the chain within 25 nm. `single_pass` still refuses taper, tabs, skims, burnout and 4-axis on a selected chain.
- `generate.rs`, `wire_verify.rs`: the calls to the new routes.

### Post

- No post script changed. `crates/post/src/agie_setup/inspection.rs:1`: the provenance line now says "our own implementation".

## The user's decisions (24 Nov 2026)

1. True arcs, no chord-only step.
2. A start hole exactly at the centre of a die circle: the lead enters towards +X. Rule: of equally near path points, the point at the least counter-clockwise angle from +X wins. A path note says so.
3. **Behaviour change for the maintainer:** TEXT, MTEXT and DIMENSION entities no longer block a selected-chain wire cut. They are not cut, and the wire is not checked against them. A path note gives the count. A HATCH (or any other skipped entity) still refuses, now by its name and count. The native Agie selected-chain door shares this check, so it also accepts a drawing with annotation.
4. Tapered (conical) arcs stay refused. Follow-up: #3941.

A punch on a circle, a racetrack or a tangent loop also takes the arc path now for the generic posts (before: a chord preview). The native Agie job (#2978, #2993) still reads its own `WireProfile`, and its goldens do not change.

**Refusal order for a selected Agie chain (review fix).** The arc door now runs before the native door for each selected chain that is not an exact polygon, also on the Agie machine. Thus the arc door's start-hole and kerf laws can refuse before the native "convex loop" refusal. Example: a lower half circle that encloses the start hole now gives "lies inside the profile". Each refusal is correct, and nothing is published. The decision file records this order.

## Readings

I read the ISO golden `wire_dxf_die_circle.nc` against the drawing (radius 5 circle, wire 0.25, gap 0.04, k = 0.165; drawing centre posts at X6 Y5):

- the lead goes from X6 Y5 to X10.835 Y5: +X, length 4.835 = 5 - 0.165;
- `G3 X1.165 Y5. I-4.835 J0.`: centre X6 Y5, end at the antipode, counter-clockwise half turn;
- `G3 X10.835 Y5. I4.835 J0.`: centre X6 Y5, back to the seam;
- `G1 X6. Y5.`: the lead-out.

I read `wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc` (the L punch, drawing turned 90 degrees): the fillet posts as `G3 X13. Y15.165 I-3.165 J0.`, centre X13 Y12 (the drawn centre), radius 3 + 0.165. Each of the four sharp outside corners has a G3 pivot of radius 0.165 about the corner. The inside corner is trimmed to X5.835 Y5.165 (k, k from the corner). The walk is counter-clockwise. The Sodick program starts the cut with a `G01` lead before its first `G03`.

## Pinning tests

- motion `wire_edm::arc_tests` (11): die circle with a centred hole (+X, two half arcs), punch circle (radial seam), line and arc punch (pivots, trim, fillet), line and arc die, inside arc under the offset refused, slot and neck refused, joint gap refused / charged to the margin, off-lattice centre snapped, mutation test (an arc 2 µm into the product fails the kerf law, chords in place of arcs fail the cover law), hole too near or on the wrong side, waste-side ring.
- sim `verify::wire::arc_tests` (3): a die circle of two half arcs passes and frees its slug; an arc 2 µm into the product is a gouge on that arc move; an arc on a leaning wire is unreadable.
- app `agie_native` `tangent::a_short_inner_offgrid_edge_or_folded_loop_publishes_nothing` (review fix, commit `6b503900f`): the lower half circle with the hole X0 Y-21 gives "lies inside the profile"; with the hole at X-19 Y-24 the arc door refuses the sharp inside corner at X14 Y-14; the upper half circle keeps the native "convex loop" refusal.
- app `wire_dxf_selection` (new module `arcs`, 3 tests, plus the changed pin `curved_pick_survives_and_is_judged_on_its_arcs_and_undo_restores_the_pick`): die circle and line and arc punch through generation, the wire laws, and the ISO, Sodick and G-EDM posts to their goldens; taper on a DXF arc refused; HATCH still refused.

## Gate

**Withdrawn:** the earlier text of this section ("1,193 steps, 1,192 ok" and the `rotary_verify` note) was wrong. It came from a log of a different branch. The quick gate on `ee7270eed` did not complete. On `ee7270eed` the review found `agie_native` red. Commit `6b503900f` fixes that test.

Head `6b503900f`, on the Mac:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (base `b13ebd4`, 30 changed files): 762 steps, 762 ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled. Wall time 57 min.
  - The plan holds by name, all ok: `app suites: agie_native` (36 tests), `wire_dxf_selection`, `g_edm_post`, the four `sodick_*` app suites, each `wire_*` app suite, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `post suites: script_agie_native`, `script_sodick_wire`, `motion suites: lib`, `sim suites: lib`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `6b503900f`: clean.
- On `ee7270eed` (the review fix changes only one test and the decision file): `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/main`: 6 steps, all ok. Targeted runs: motion `wire_edm` lib 72 ok, sim `verify::wire` 29 ok, app `wire_dxf_selection` 6 ok.
- Suites that assert a refusal text of a selected-chain door (grep for "convex loop", "lies inside the profile", "start hole", "selected chain"): `agie_native`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `wire_contour`, `wire_post`, `wire_verify`, `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_4axis`, `sodick_wire_passes`, `sodick_wire_post`, `golden_cl`, `tool_dxf_profile`, post `agie_safe_setup`, `script_agie_native`. Each is ok. Post `agie_safe_setup` is not in the quick plan; I ran it by name on `6b503900f` (`cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup`: 22 ok). The others are in the quick plan above.

Heavy step (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches `app heavy: wire_dxf_selection`, `wire_post` and `wire_stamp`. None of these binaries, and no module of `motion::wire_edm` or `sim::verify::wire`, has an `#[ignore]` heavy test. No heavy test covers this code, so no targeted heavy step exists.

## Not exercised

- No control ran these programs. The goldens are read against the drawing only.
- Tabs, skims, burnout, taper and 4-axis on a DXF chain stay refused (as before). #3617 works on skims and the closing overlap in the same files.
- A short span that an inside trim consumes (for example a short chamfer in a tight inside corner) is refused, not removed.
- Model-based wire cuts still post chords (#3215).

## Goldens moved

All new, none changed:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc`, `.../wire-iso/wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sodick-wire/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc`, `.../sodick-wire/wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/g-edm/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc`, `.../g-edm/wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`

Reason: the first arc output of the selected-chain wire path, for each post that writes arcs.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/3937-wire-dxf-arcs.md`.

Changelog: Wire Contour on a selected DXF chain cuts arcs and circles as true G2/G3 arcs (die and punch), with a stated +X entry from the centre of a circle; TEXT, MTEXT and DIMENSION entities no longer block the cut.

Effort: max

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Refs #3215
Fixes #3937
